journeys.content_focus: Catalysts, activation energy, active-site compatibility, induced fit, and enzyme reuse
journeys.setting_logic: A molecular workshop makes the reaction barrier, docking geometry, and catalytic turnover visible before terminology is attached.

journeys.premise: A reaction workshop is wasting energy because its molecular jobs have been reduced to labels. The learner must rebuild catalysis by comparing reaction barriers, docking a real substrate at an active site, and watching the same enzyme return to service after product release.
journeys.mission: Follow one reaction from activation-energy barrier to enzyme-substrate binding and catalytic turnover so enzyme action is understood as a reusable molecular mechanism.
journeys.stakes: If the workshop remains vague, later regulation scenes will collapse into memorized inhibitor names without a working model of what an enzyme actually does.
journeys.continuity_object: one amber substrate token that is tracked from free reactant to active-site binding, conversion, product release, and enzyme reset
journeys.opening_image: Two reaction tracks rise ahead: one climbs a high energy hill while a second passes through a lower enzyme-controlled route.
journeys.ending_payoff: The amber substrate is converted, the products leave, and the unchanged enzyme station resets for another cycle.
narrative_constraints: The learner always knows where they are relative to the previous locus and can redraw the route from memory.

journeys.setting_logic: A control wing allows one enzyme system to be stressed, supplied, blocked, activated, and regulated while preserving clear distinctions among mechanisms.

journeys.premise: The enzyme control wing is producing erratic rates. One reference enzyme is carried through heat, pH, concentration, helper, inhibitor, allosteric, cooperative, and pathway-feedback tests so each regulatory mechanism remains physically distinct.
journeys.mission: Stress and regulate one enzyme system while preserving the difference between altered protein structure, active-site competition, allosteric control, cooperative binding, feedback inhibition, and irreversible loss of function.
journeys.stakes: Students must be able to diagnose why enzyme activity changed from evidence rather than attaching every rate change to denaturation or inhibition.
journeys.continuity_object: a transparent reference enzyme whose active site and overall conformation remain visible at every control station
journeys.opening_image: A transparent enzyme glows in a central clamp while temperature, pH, substrate, helper, and inhibitor controls surround it.
journeys.ending_payoff: The control wing stabilizes only after every mechanism has a distinct physical cause and a distinct visible consequence.

journeys.content_focus: Metabolism, thermodynamics, free energy, cellular work, ATP structure, coupling, and regeneration
journeys.setting_logic: An energy-accounting hall keeps forms of energy, thermodynamic constraints, work, and ATP cycling inside one causal system instead of treating them as separate definitions.

journeys.premise: An energy-exchange hall has lost its accounting system. Metabolic routes, energy forms, thermodynamic constraints, cellular work, and ATP cycling must be reconnected into one lawful energy-flow system.
journeys.mission: Trace how cells transform energy, remain organized while increasing total entropy, couple favorable and unfavorable processes, and continuously regenerate ATP.
journeys.stakes: Without a coherent energy model, photosynthesis and respiration become disconnected pathway lists instead of transformations constrained by thermodynamics.
journeys.continuity_object: a glowing energy token whose form changes while the ledger always tracks where energy enters, changes form, performs work, and disperses
journeys.opening_image: A wall-sized metabolic map flickers beside a dark energy ledger, while an ATP wheel has stopped mid-turn.
journeys.ending_payoff: The ledger balances, ATP cycles again, and the same metabolic logic can be recognized across widely separated organisms.

journeys.setting_logic: A light-processing conservatory follows energy from incoming photons through pigments, photosystems, electron transfer, proton-gradient formation, ATP, and NADPH.

journeys.premise: A light-capture conservatory is receiving sunlight but cannot reliably convert it into ATP and NADPH. The learner follows light from ecological context into leaf and chloroplast structure, pigments, photosystems, electron transfer, proton-gradient formation, and photophosphorylation.
journeys.mission: Build one continuous map from photon capture to linear electron flow and the chemical energy products that leave the light reactions.
journeys.stakes: The learner must know which events happen in which chloroplast structures and must keep excitation-energy transfer separate from electron transfer.
journeys.continuity_object: one pulse of absorbed light followed by one highlighted electron path and one rising thylakoid proton-gradient gauge
journeys.opening_image: A beam of white light enters a glasshouse, passes through a leaf, and breaks into a spectrum above a transparent chloroplast.
journeys.ending_payoff: ATP and NADPH leave the thylakoid system together, ready to power carbon fixation in the adjoining greenhouse.

journeys.content_focus: Calvin cycle, carbon fixation, Rubisco, RuBP, G3P, photorespiration, C4, and CAM
journeys.setting_logic: A carbon greenhouse turns ATP and NADPH into visible carbon-flow work, then tests how plants reduce photorespiration under different environmental constraints.

journeys.premise: The carbon-fixation greenhouse has ATP and NADPH available but carbon output falls whenever conditions favor photorespiration. The learner reconstructs the Calvin cycle and then compares two carbon-concentrating strategies.
journeys.mission: Follow carbon from CO2 fixation through G3P output and RuBP regeneration, then diagnose Rubisco oxygenation and compare C4 spatial separation with CAM temporal separation.
journeys.stakes: Students must understand the logic of carbon fixation without being forced to memorize every Calvin-cycle intermediate.
journeys.continuity_object: one carbon tracer that enters as CO2, appears in fixed carbon, contributes to G3P, and is contrasted with the photorespiratory detour
journeys.opening_image: A green circular workbench waits in the stroma while ATP and NADPH arrive from the light-capture conservatory.
journeys.ending_payoff: The greenhouse restores carbon gain by correctly identifying carbon fixation, photorespiration, and the contrasting C4 and CAM solutions.

journeys.content_focus: Aerobic respiration from fuel intake through glycolysis, mitochondrial oxidation, electron transport, proton gradients, ATP synthase, heat, and prokaryotic respiration

journeys.premise: A respiration power plant has fuel but its energy harvest is fragmented. The learner follows carbon and electrons from cytosolic glycolysis into mitochondrial oxidation, the electron-transport chain, proton pumping, oxygen reduction, ATP synthase, heat, and a prokaryotic membrane comparison.
journeys.mission: Reconstruct aerobic respiration as a coordinated sequence that transfers energy from fuel to reduced carriers, a proton-motive force, and ATP.
journeys.stakes: The learner must keep carbon flow, electron flow, proton movement, compartment geography, and phosphorylation mechanisms separate but causally connected.
journeys.continuity_object: a paired tracer system: a carbon token follows fuel oxidation while a blue electron token is transferred to carriers and finally to the respiratory ETC
journeys.opening_image: A glucose shipment enters a power plant whose carbon line, electron line, and proton-pressure gauges are all disconnected.
journeys.ending_payoff: The plant produces ATP with a stable proton gradient, oxygen accepts terminal electrons, and the learner can reconstruct the same membrane logic in a prokaryote.

journeys.content_focus: Aerobic versus anaerobic respiration, fermentation, NAD+ recycling, alcohol fermentation, and lactate metabolism
journeys.setting_logic: A branching annex compares alternative routes from shared metabolic constraints so anaerobic respiration and fermentation cannot collapse into the same idea.

journeys.premise: The alternative-energy annex receives cells that cannot rely on the ordinary oxygen-terminal route. The learner must separate anaerobic respiration from fermentation and then use redox bookkeeping to explain alcohol and lactate pathways.
journeys.mission: Compare alternative terminal electron-acceptor routes with fermentation, then follow NAD+ recycling through alcohol and lactate fermentation without importing outdated lactate misconceptions.
journeys.stakes: Students must not collapse anaerobic respiration, fermentation, oxygen absence, and lactate physiology into one undifferentiated idea.
journeys.continuity_object: a limited pool of NAD+ cards that must be regenerated so glycolysis can continue
journeys.opening_image: Three route signs branch from the same glycolysis platform while the NAD+ card rack is nearly empty.
journeys.ending_payoff: The NAD+ cards return to glycolysis through clearly distinct pathways, and lactate is left as a transportable metabolic intermediate rather than a “muscle poison.”
